title_candidates: They Filmed Her When She Hid — Now They Can't Look Away
The Girl Behind the Curtain Was the Story Everyone Wanted
He Knew Her Before the World Called Her Beautiful
logline: In an elite performing-arts academy built inside a converted railway station, Mina, a scholarship stagehand who writes plays in empty lighting booths but hides behind black crew clothes after being mocked as the 'invisible stage rat' is pushed toward public transformation, but the love interest is credible only because he witnessed her courage before the world approved of her.
audience_promise: A mobile-native transformation romance in which public gaze inversion, pre-transformation witness, behavioral cost, reciprocal memory debt, and a second performance engine turn visibility into agency rather than mere makeover reward.

emotional_engine.wound: Mina learned that visibility is dangerous because her aunt made Mina wear oversized clothes and stay backstage after her mother was harassed for being too visible on stage; public misreading then confirmed the shame.
emotional_engine.want: remain useful and safe without becoming a spectacle again
emotional_engine.need: claim authorship, visibility, and love without treating appearance approval as proof of worth
emotional_engine.injustice: Vega, a legacy performer whose family funds the academy's new student film converts status insecurity into public humiliation and image control
emotional_engine.protective_counterforce: Aren, the academy's withdrawn lighting designer who once watched Mina calm a panicking child performer before anyone knew she wrote the play protects the person before the transformation because Aren remembers Mina's anonymous voice guiding a child performer through a blackout and values her courage before her appearance changes
emotional_engine.belonging_payoff: the staircase that once turned her into a spectacle becomes the place where she speaks as author rather than object of attention
emotional_engine.secret_or_power_asymmetry: legacy status, image control, and institutional casting power oppose a scholarship protagonist with no public protection
emotional_engine.cost_of_failure: she retreats into hiding, loses authorship/professional agency, and confirms the false belief that visibility is annihilation

protagonist.identity: Mina, a scholarship stagehand who writes plays in empty lighting booths but hides behind black crew clothes after being mocked as the 'invisible stage rat'
protagonist.vulnerability: public shame, image control, family fear, and lack of institutional power
protagonist.capability: craft/professional competence, protective courage, persistence, and the ability to lead others once she stops hiding
protagonist.agency_first_action: she protects or guides a vulnerable person before protecting her image
protagonist.transformation: from protected invisibility to chosen visibility grounded in authorship, competence, consent, and reciprocal recognition

opening_event.first_10_seconds: a future-pressure fragment inside a student film adaptation of a masked heroine story that forces Mina to perform visibility rather than merely receive admiration hints that powerful people need the hidden protagonist before the story cuts back to the wound
opening_event.first_60_seconds: Mina is spatially trapped in the station-hall staircase where students gather, film, whisper, and later applaud while others film, laugh, or misread her silence
opening_event.first_5_minutes: the family fear system, the meaning-carrier cracked brass backstage key, and the first pre-transformation protective act are established before the visual transformation
opening_event.dramatic_question: can a protagonist who learned that visibility is dangerous become publicly seen without surrendering authorship or accepting shallow approval?

theme_lane.family_or_heir_hook: protection itself becomes the wound when a family teaches a child to hide in order to survive
theme_lane.romance_hook: Aren, the academy's withdrawn lighting designer who once watched Mina calm a panicking child performer before anyone knew she wrote the play remembers reciprocal courage rather than rewarding beauty
theme_lane.modern_power_hook: viral spectatorship, legacy status, institutional casting, and public image control

transformation_engine.family_protection_wound: her aunt made Mina wear oversized clothes and stay backstage after her mother was harassed for being too visible on stage
transformation_engine.pre_transformation_witness: Aren remembers Mina's anonymous voice guiding a child performer through a blackout and values her courage before her appearance changes
transformation_engine.reciprocal_memory_debt: years earlier Mina protected Aren from older students who scattered his lighting notes; he never forgot that she was brave before anyone admired her
transformation_engine.behavioral_transformation_cost: speech practice, movement training, authorship workshops, and repeated threshold-crossing rather than a cosmetic montage alone
transformation_engine.second_performance_engine: a student film adaptation of a masked heroine story that forces Mina to perform visibility rather than merely receive admiration
transformation_engine.agency_violation: the director and Mina's aunt agree to cast her before asking whether she consents
transformation_engine.public_space_reversal: the station-hall staircase where students gather, film, whisper, and later applaud
transformation_engine.closure: the staircase that once turned her into a spectacle becomes the place where she speaks as author rather than object of attention

nearest_failures: makeover treated as proof of worth
love interest attracted only after transformation
public humiliation without systemic cause or spatial closure
second half repeating jealousy rather than opening a new performance/professional engine
self-destructive despair imagery used as a cheap transformation trigger
mitigations: show transformation as behavior and skill, not only appearance
open a second professional/performance engine after the reveal
make consent violations by allies visible and consequential
counterexamples_checked: beautiful transformation imagery alone does not explain retention
romantic rescue is weak unless reciprocal and pre-transformation
viral attention can repeat the wound rather than repair it

packaging.thumbnail_single_read: Mina centered between public approval and a hostile rival while cracked brass backstage key catches the light
packaging.curiosity_gap: who saw her before the world decided she was worth watching?
packaging.visual_before_after: hidden backstage/pool-floor posture becomes upright public authorship in the same space
packaging.title_thumbnail_mismatch_risk: generic beauty packaging would undersell authorship, consent, and pre-transformation recognition

evidence_boundaries: Inspired by mechanism-level evidence in the EchoDrama Hidden Beauty deep dive; characters, institutions, object, second engine, and ending are original.
No CTR, retention, or traffic causality is claimed from public video metadata.

meaning_carrier.opening_meaning: the key opens the lighting booth where Mina secretly writes and where her mother once hid during harassment
meaning_carrier.closing_reversal: the same key opens the booth publicly so Mina can claim authorship and choose visibility on her own terms
meaning_carrier.final_sequence_use: the object is used openly in the final authorship/rescue ritual inside the station-hall staircase where students gather, film, whisper, and later applaud

relational_contract.power_asymmetry: legacy visibility/status power versus scholarship protagonist with no control over her public image
relational_contract.safety_or_kindness_before_power: Aren remembers Mina's anonymous voice guiding a child performer through a blackout and values her courage before her appearance changes
relational_contract.costly_protagonist_action: she protects a vulnerable person before protecting her appearance or reputation
relational_contract.consent_or_personhood_repair: allies must return authorship and ask consent after trying to arrange her visibility for her
relational_contract.payoff_image: the staircase that once turned her into a spectacle becomes the place where she speaks as author rather than object of attention
